title: Longest One-Way Run
statement:
You get an integer array nums. A one-way run is a contiguous block where every value is strictly larger than the one before it, or every value is strictly smaller than the one before it.

Return the length of the longest one-way run. A single value is a run of length 1. Two equal neighbours can never be in the same run.

examples.why: [5, 4, 1] falls the whole way. [2, 5, 5] is not a run because 5 = 5 is not strictly larger.
No pair of neighbours differs, so each value is a run on its own.
[2, 4, 6, 8]. There are five upward steps in total, but they are not all next to each other.

hints: Walk left to right. When you look at nums[i] and nums[i − 1], which runs can continue and which must restart?
Keep two lengths: the rising run ending at i and the falling run ending at i.
If nums[i] > nums[i − 1] the rising length grows by 1 and the falling one resets to 1; mirror that for <; on equality both reset to 1. The answer is the largest length seen.

explain.intuition:
Every run ends somewhere. At position i, the longest rising run ending there is one longer than the one ending at i − 1 if the step up is strict, and just 1 otherwise. The same goes for falling runs. So two counters carried along the array describe everything, and the answer is the biggest value either counter ever reaches.

Equal neighbours are the case people miss. They break a rising run and a falling run at the same time, so both counters restart at 1.
steps: For each i from 1: if nums[i] > nums[i − 1], set up++ and down = 1.
If nums[i] < nums[i − 1], set down++ and up = 1. If equal, set both to 1.
pitfalls: Using ≥ instead of >. Then [1, 2, 2, 3, 4] returns 5 instead of 3.
Forgetting to reset the other counter. A rise must end any falling run, otherwise a zig-zag keeps growing.
Counting steps instead of values: a run with k steps has k + 1 values.

solutions.title: Extend from every start
solutions.idea: From each index, extend a rising run and a falling run as far as they go.

solutions.title: Two counters in one pass
solutions.idea: Carry the length of the rising and the falling run that end at the current index.

followups: Allow equal neighbours inside a run (non-strict). Which line changes?
Return the longest run that rises and then falls (a single peak).
